title: Helm rollback for match-engine, ingest-api, and break-svc
subtitle: Cold-execute from a laptop. Schema forward-fix versus rollback. Hooks and CRDs that helm leaves behind. January rebalance as the worked example.
author: Aman Kumar
audience: On-call SE II and Diego Alvarez (SRE). Priya Nair if you are about to roll a migrate.
owners: Aman Kumar (charts), Diego Alvarez (cluster clh-prod-eks-01), Kavya Menon (match-engine migrate jobs)
summary: How to helm rollback match-engine, ingest-api, or break-svc on clh-prod-eks-01 without making a bad deploy worse. Read the preconditions first: if a schema migrate already applied, rollback of the chart is often the wrong move and you forward-fix instead. Commands below are copy-paste. After rollback, check for leftover Jobs, failed helm hooks, and CRDs that helm does not delete. Worked example is the January 11, 2024 rebalance (CLH-INC-2024-017), where we rolled match-engine 1.44.2 to 1.43.9 and then spent 41 minutes cleaning a migrate Job that had already added break.leg_status.consumer_epoch. Written so a cold on-call can execute it at 02:00 ET.
form_description: Internal helm rollback runbook for three Clearhaven production charts. Covers schema preconditions, exact commands, leftover hook and CRD checks, and a worked example from the January 2024 rebalance incident.
revision_history: Notes from CLH-INC-2024-017, not yet a runbook.
First full draft after Priya asked for a cold-execute doc. Diego reviewed the kubectl bits.
Added CRD leftover section and the --wait timeout we actually use.
Approved. Worked example numbers checked against the incident timeline.

blocks.text: Read this before you type helm rollback

blocks.label: Decision rule
blocks.text: Rollback the chart only if the running pods are the problem and the schema on clh-recon-prod is still compatible with the previous image. If a migrate Job in this release already succeeded, do not helm rollback. Forward-fix the image or follow CLH-SOP-2024-011 to down-migrate, which is a Priya call, not an on-call call. If you are not sure whether the migrate ran, you are not ready to rollback. Check flyway_schema_history first.
This runbook covers three Helm releases on cluster clh-prod-eks-01, account 184920337661, region us-east-1:

blocks.caption: Production Helm releases. History is helm history, not git.

blocks.text: kubecontext: arn:aws:eks:us-east-1:184920337661:cluster/clh-prod-eks-01. If your laptop says something else, stop. Staging is clh-staging-eks-01. Rolling staging in a panic is how we got a sticky assignor into prod by accident in May 2023. Do not.

I wrote this because helm rollback is three tokens and people treat it like undo. It is not undo. Helm re-applies the previous release's manifests. It does not un-run SQL. It does not delete CRDs. It does not always delete hook Jobs. The January rebalance is the example at the bottom; if you only read one narrative, read that. If you only execute, start at Preconditions.
When this runbook applies

items: A helm upgrade --install you or CI just did is CrashLoop, ImagePull, or failing /healthz, and the previous revision was healthy for at least 2 hours before the upgrade.
Error budget burn on match-engine-prod or ingest-api-prod started within 15 minutes of a chart change (check #clh-deploys, not just your memory).
Helen Cho reports exception queue depth jumping in the same window as a deploy (she will say the time in ET; believe her).
You are on-call, it is night, and Priya is not answering yet. This doc is the path that does not wait on her, as long as the migrate did not run.

blocks.text: When it does not apply. Kafka lag with no recent helm history: that is CLH-RB-2023-012. OOM on a nested RailClear file: CLH-RB-2024-007. RDS failover: CLH-RB-2024-015. A bad configmap you can helm upgrade --reuse-values --set without going backwards: do that, do not rollback. Rollback is for 'the revision itself is poison.'
Preconditions (do these, in this order)

items: Confirm cluster and namespace. aws eks update-kubeconfig --name clh-prod-eks-01 --region us-east-1 --profile clh-prod. kubectl config current-context must show 184920337661 and clh-prod-eks-01.
Confirm you are the on-call or Priya/Diego asked you. Post in #clh-deploys: 'considering helm rollback <release> n->n-1, checking migrate first.'

helm history <release> -n <ns> --max 5. Note the current REVISION, STATUS, CHART version, and DESCRIPTION. You need the current number and the previous deployed number. A revision in STATUS failed is not always the one to roll to.
Check whether this upgrade ran a migrate. kubectl -n <ns> get jobs | grep migrate. Then kubectl -n <ns> logs job/<name> --tail=80. Look for flyway 'Successfully applied' or a SQLException.
If the migrate Job succeeded, stop. Go to 'Rollback is the wrong move.' Do not run helm rollback yet.

If there is no migrate Job, or the Job never created (hook failed before SQL), or the Job is still Running and you can delete it before it applies, continue. Deleting a Running migrate Job is allowed only if logs show it has not reached 'Migrating schema'. If it has, treat as succeeded and stop.

Check schema anyway. psql against clh-recon-prod as role oncall_ro, query flyway_schema_history ORDER BY installed_rank DESC LIMIT 8. Compare installed_rank and version to the previous chart's expected version (table below). If prod schema is ahead of the previous image, stop.

Diego or the on-call SRE: confirm you are not in a cluster-autoscaler scale-down or a node drain. helm rollback during a drain looks like a rollback failure. kubectl -n clh-match get nodes is the wrong command; kubectl get nodes --label-columns=topology.kubernetes.io/zone and look for SchedulingDisabled.

blocks.caption: flyway versions the previous images expect. If prod is higher than this, the old image may boot and then throw on missing columns, or worse, write nulls. Update this table when you cut a migrate. Last checked August 27, 2024.
headers: Safe to roll to that image?
rows: yes, if you are rolling 1.51.4 -> 1.51.3 and 1.51.4 did not ship V45
NO. Do not roll to January. Schema has moved.
yes, break-svc has no migrate. Still check it does not require a match-engine proto that the rolled match-engine no longer serves.

blocks.label: Schema is not helm history
blocks.text: flyway_schema_history lives on clh-recon-prod.cluster-c8a1.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com, database recon, schema public. Helm history lives in Secrets in the namespace. They diverge every time a migrate Job succeeds and you later helm rollback the Deployment. January 11 they diverged by one version for 41 minutes. That is the incident. Read the worked example before you invent a third state.
Commands: identify revision

blocks.caption: History and live objects. Run all three even if you only plan to roll one release. January we rolled match-engine and missed that ingest-api had also moved 4 minutes earlier.
blocks.text:
export CTX=arn:aws:eks:us-east-1:184920337661:cluster/clh-prod-eks-01
kubectl config use-context "$CTX"

helm history match-engine -n clh-match --max 8
helm history ingest-api -n clh-ingest --max 8
helm history break-svc -n clh-break --max 8

# current objects
kubectl -n clh-match get deploy,po,job,cm,secret -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=match-engine
kubectl -n clh-ingest get deploy,po,job,cm,secret -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=ingest-api
kubectl -n clh-break get deploy,po,job,cm,secret -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=break-svc

# hook leftovers (helm labels these with hook policy)
kubectl -n clh-match get job,po -l 'helm.sh/hook'
kubectl -n clh-ingest get job,po -l 'helm.sh/hook'
kubectl -n clh-break get job,po -l 'helm.sh/hook'

# what the Deployment thinks it is running
kubectl -n clh-match get deploy match-engine -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}{" "}{.status.observedGeneration}\n'
kubectl -n clh-ingest get deploy ingest-api -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}{" "}{.status.observedGeneration}\n'
kubectl -n clh-break get deploy break-svc -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}{" "}{.status.observedGeneration}\n'
Commands: rollback (only after preconditions pass)

Default: roll to the previous deployed revision, not to an arbitrary old one. helm rollback <name> [REVISION]. If you omit REVISION it uses current-1, which is wrong when current-1 is a failed revision that never became healthy. Look at helm history STATUS. You want the last revision with STATUS deployed that was also healthy in Datadog for 2+ hours. In January, revision 22 was deployed and sick; revision 21 was deployed and healthy. We rolled to 21 by number, not by default current-1, because there was a 22.1 retry in between that helm recorded as 23 failed. Default current-1 would have landed on 23. Type the number.

blocks.caption: Rollback one release. Timeouts are the ones Diego measured. Do not drop --wait so you can 'get back to Kafka.' You will miss a hung rollout.
blocks.text:
# example: match-engine current 48, last good 47
helm rollback match-engine 47 -n clh-match --wait --timeout 10m --cleanup-on-fail

# ingest-api
helm rollback ingest-api 31 -n clh-ingest --wait --timeout 8m --cleanup-on-fail

# break-svc (faster, no migrate)
helm rollback break-svc 18 -n clh-break --wait --timeout 6m --cleanup-on-fail

# watch
kubectl -n clh-match rollout status deploy/match-engine --timeout=10m
kubectl -n clh-match get po -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=match-engine -o wide

# smoke (from laptop, prod VPN or the jump pod)
kubectl -n clh-match exec deploy/match-engine -- curl -sS --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:8081/healthz
# expect {"status":"ok","flyway":"44","consumer":"match-engine-prod"}

kubectl -n clh-ingest exec deploy/ingest-api -- curl -sS --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz
# expect {"status":"ok","broker":"clh-msk-prod","lag_ms":<400}

# break-svc
kubectl -n clh-break exec deploy/break-svc -- curl -sS --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:8082/healthz

If --wait times out. Do not immediately rollback again. kubectl -n clh-match describe deploy/match-engine and look for ProgressDeadlineExceeded vs a pod in CrashLoop. ProgressDeadlineExceeded after a rollback often means the new (old) ReplicaSet cannot schedule: node pressure, or anti-affinity, or the previous image is no longer in ECR. ECR lifecycle on clh/match-engine keeps 30 tags. 1.43.9 is gone. 1.51.3 is there. If the image is missing you cannot rollback to it. Forward-fix or re-tag from the backup repo ecr-backup.prod.clearhaven.internal, which Jordan Hale owns. Page Jordan, do not docker tag from your laptop into prod.
How to tell if a CRD or hook left junk

Helm 3 does not delete CRDs on rollback or uninstall. We have two CRDs that charts touch: matchengines.platform.clearhaven.internal (MatchEngineConfig, installed by match-engine chart as a crd/ hook, install-only) and ingressroutes.traefik.io (cluster-scoped, Diego's traefik chart, not ours, but our charts create IngressRoute objects). Rollback re-applies the previous IngressRoute. It does not remove an IngressRoute you added in the bad revision if the previous chart did not contain that object. Helm three-way merge is supposed to, and sometimes does not when the object was created by a hook.

blocks.caption: Leftover hunt. Run after every rollback, even if /healthz is green. January we had a green /healthz and a hook Job still applying V39.
blocks.text:
# Jobs that should not be sitting around
kubectl -n clh-match get jobs
kubectl -n clh-ingest get jobs
# COMPLETED migrate from a rolled-back release is junk. Delete it so the next upgrade does not get confused by the name.
# helm hook delete-policy is hook-succeeded,before-hook-creation on current charts.
# older charts (pre-1.44) used hook-succeeded only, so a failed migrate Job blocks the next hook.

kubectl -n clh-match delete job match-engine-migrate --ignore-not-found
# only if you have confirmed it is leftover AND flyway already recorded the version, or the Job never reached SQL

# failed hooks leave pods in Failed/Error
kubectl -n clh-match get po --field-selector=status.phase==Failed
kubectl -n clh-match delete po -l 'helm.sh/hook' --field-selector=status.phase==Failed

# CRDs (cluster scoped). Do not delete the CRD. Do delete extra CRs from the bad rev.
kubectl get crd | grep -i clearhaven
kubectl get matchengines.platform.clearhaven.internal -A
kubectl -n clh-match get matchengines -o yaml
# expect one object: match-engine-prod. If you see match-engine-canary from a hook, that is junk from 1.44.2.
# kubectl -n clh-match delete matchengine match-engine-canary

# IngressRoute extras
kubectl -n clh-match get ingressroute
kubectl -n clh-ingest get ingressroute
# names should match the values-prod.yaml service names. Extra names from a canary annotation are junk.

# helm metadata vs live
helm get manifest match-engine -n clh-match > /tmp/me-manifest.yaml
kubectl -n clh-match get deploy,svc,ingressroute,job,cm -o yaml > /tmp/me-live.yaml
# diff those if something still looks wrong. You will not finish the diff at 02:00. You will grep for canary and for 1.44.2.

ConfigMaps. match-engine mounts cm/match-engine-flags. A rollback restores the previous ConfigMap body. Pods do not reload it unless they restart. --wait on helm rollback should recreate pods. If someone set checksum annotations off (we did that in March 2024 for a debugging session, CH-REL-2204, and Kavya turned them back on), pods can be running new flags from a mutated ConfigMap with an old image, or the reverse. After rollback: kubectl -n clh-match get cm match-engine-flags -o yaml | grep consumer.epoch and confirm it matches the image you rolled to. If it does not, helm rollback did not touch the ConfigMap because it was --reuse-values mutated out of band. Then you have to helm upgrade --values values-prod.yaml to the old chart, not a second rollback.
Hook policies we actually ship

rows: Failed Job named match-engine-migrate blocks next upgrade. Pod in Error.
COMPLETED Job hanging around. Harmless. Delete when you see it after a rollback so history is readable.
Rare. Only on a new namespace. If it failed, CRD may be half-applied. Page Diego.
You should not see this on a rollback. If you do, someone ran helm uninstall. Stop and call Priya.

blocks.text: When rollback is the wrong move (failed or succeeded migrate)
Two cases, both 'do not helm rollback,' different next actions.
Migrate succeeded, app is bad

flyway_schema_history has a new version. The Deployment is CrashLoop or serving wrong answers. Rolling the Deployment back to an image that does not know the new column is a coin flip: the old JDBC code may ignore extra columns (fine) or it may SELECT * into a struct and blow up (match-engine 1.44 did this with consumer_epoch). You do not know which at 02:00 unless you already tested that pair. We do not keep a compatibility matrix. So we do not roll. We forward-fix: revert the Java change, keep the column, ship a new tag, helm upgrade forward. Priya wants a ticket before you helm upgrade again, even a revert, so the history is not rollback-upgrade-rollback. Ticket, tag, upgrade. Time cost is 18-40 minutes if CI is green. That is still faster than the January 41-minute cleanup.
Migrate failed halfway

Job logs show a SQLException. flyway_schema_history may have a row with success=false. Postgres may have a lock or a half-added column. helm rollback will put the old Deployment back while the schema is dirty. The old image may boot. Then the next migrate (even a retry of the same version) fails because the column exists. This is CLH-SOP-2024-011, not this runbook. Short version for 02:00: do not helm rollback. Leave the new Deployment at 0 replicas if you have to (kubectl -n clh-match scale deploy/match-engine --replicas=0) so it stops writing, keep the old ReplicaSet if it is still around (it may not be, helm --wait may have deleted it), and page Kavya plus Diego. Do not run flyway repair from your laptop unless Kavya is on the call. repair without her is how we got two V39 rows in staging in June.

blocks.caption: What to do vs what not to do, migrate edition.
rows: Job never created, pods CrashLoop on image pull
Job created, logs never got past 'Waiting for Postgres', Job deleted by you
Job 'Successfully applied V45', pods CrashLoop on Unknown column in mapper
Forward-fix image that knows V45, or maps around it. Ticket + helm upgrade.
Job SQLException, success=false in flyway, column half-there
CLH-SOP-2024-011. Scale to 0 if it is writing garbage. Page Kavya.
No Job (break-svc), bad config, previous rev healthy
Rollback break-svc. Confirm match-engine proto still matches.
You want last week's chart because today's Kafka is sad
Wrong runbook. CLH-RB-2023-012. Helm will not fix lag.

blocks.text: Worked example: January 11, 2024 rebalance (CLH-INC-2024-017)

This is the incident that made Priya ask for a runbook instead of a Slack thread. Times ET. I was on-call. Diego joined at 06:51. Kavya joined at 07:04. Helen was already in #clh-ops because exception depth had gone from 280 to 4,116 between 06:20 and 06:44.

What we had shipped. Overnight CI, helm upgrade match-engine 1.44.2, revision 22, started 06:12, --wait said happy at 06:18. Chart change: cooperative sticky assignor (good, we wanted it) plus migrate V39 which added break.leg_status.consumer_epoch (integer, default 0) so the new consumer could fence old members during a rebalance. The migrate Job ran at 06:12:40, applied V39 in 2.1 seconds, Job marked complete. Nobody in #clh-deploys said 'migrate ran.' The description field in helm history was 'Upgrade complete.' That is the default. It does not mention SQL.

What broke. 1.44.2 had a bug in the sticky assignor wrapper: max.poll.interval.ms was still 300000, session.timeout.ms 45000, and the fence on consumer_epoch ran inside poll(), which on a 12-pod group during the upgrade rebalance took 11.4 seconds extra per member. Members got kicked, rejoined, fenced each other. Rebalance loop. Lag on clh.settlement.inbound climbed from 2.4k to 1.82M by 06:40. Match-ack stalled. Helen's queue filled with EXC-HOLD because match-engine was alive and saying 'waiting for epoch' on 38.6% of legs.

What I did wrong. At 06:44 I ran helm rollback match-engine -n clh-match --wait without a revision number. helm history at that moment was: 21 deployed (1.43.9, good), 22 deployed (1.44.2, bad). current-1 was 21. That part lucked out. --wait completed at 06:53. Pods came up on 1.43.9. /healthz was ok. Lag started to drain. I posted 'rolled back, draining.' I did not look at flyway. I did not delete the migrate Job. The Job was COMPLETED, named match-engine-migrate, still in the namespace.

What happened next. 1.43.9 does not know consumer_epoch. Hibernate with a naming strategy that maps all columns on leg_status tried to read consumer_epoch into a field that did not exist in the entity. That path is not /healthz. It is the match write path. At 06:57 error rate on match-engine.write hit 82%. Pods did not CrashLoop. They served 500s on writes and 200s on health. Lag drain reversed. Diego noticed the Hibernate error at 07:01 in Datadog, not in kubectl. Kavya queried flyway at 07:06: V39 installed_rank 39, success true, installed_on 06:12:42. Schema was ahead of the image I had just rolled to.

rows: helm upgrade 1.44.2 starts, migrate Job applies V39
Kavya finds V39, we stop rolling
helm upgrade 1.44.3 (assignor bug reverted, entity knows consumer_epoch)
Rev 23 was a failed attempt that omitted --wait
Cleanup: delete leftover Job, delete match-engine-canary CR

blocks.text: The leftover CR. 1.44.2 chart had a hook that created MatchEngineConfig/match-engine-canary for a shadow consumer we never turned on. Rollback to 1.43.9 did not delete it, because 1.43.9's chart did not know the object, and the hook had already succeeded. At 08:16 Diego found it while grepping CRs. The canary object pointed at consumer group match-engine-canary, which did not exist. Harmless, confusing in kubectl get matchengines. We deleted it. The chart in 1.51 no longer creates that object. If you see it, it is fossil, delete it.

The leftover Job. match-engine-migrate COMPLETED from 06:12 sat until 08:18. I deleted it after Kavya confirmed V39 was the desired schema. If we had upgraded again with the old hook policy (hook-succeeded only, no before-hook-creation), the next migrate Job would have failed to create because the name was taken. 1.44.3 already had before-hook-creation. We still deleted it so helm history and kubectl get jobs agreed.

What we should have done at 06:44. Seen the migrate Job complete. Queried flyway. Seen V39. Not rolled. Scale 1.44.2 to 12 was already done; the fix was a one-line revert of the assignor wrapper, keep the entity field, ship 1.44.3. That is what we did at 07:22, 38 minutes later, after a detour through a green /healthz that was lying. The detour was this runbook's reason to exist.

blocks.label: Copy this into the Sev-2 notes if you rollback
blocks.text: Template: 'helm history <rel> before: rev N <chart> <status>. flyway: Vx success=<t/f> at <time>. migrate Job: <exists/logs>. Action: rollback to rev M / forward-fix <tag> / scale 0 and page Kavya. Leftover check: jobs, failed hook pods, matchengines CR, ingressroute extras. smoke: /healthz AND a write path (not health only).' January we had health only. Do both.
Failure modes after a 'successful' rollback
Health 200, writes failing

January. Hibernate or a column mapper. Check match-engine logs for SQLException, break-svc for UNAVAILABLE on gRPC, ingest-api for 23505 unique_violation if a sequence moved. Smoke must include a write. For match-engine, the smoke Job (post-upgrade hook) does. helm rollback does not re-run post-upgrade hooks. So the smoke Job will not run unless you kubectl create job --from=cronjob/match-engine-smoke (we have a CronJob now, 1.51) or curl the internal /debug/write-probe which only works from inside the cluster. Use the CronJob: kubectl -n clh-match create job --from=cronjob/match-engine-smoke smoke-manual-$(date +%H%M). Wait for complete. Logs should say wrote 1 probe leg and deleted it. If the CronJob is missing (old chart), run the SQL probe Kavya left in CLH-SOP-2023-019, do not invent one.
Rollback hung on PDB

match-engine PDB minAvailable 10 of 12. A rollback that cannot evict 3 pods at once waits. --timeout 10m then fails, leaving two ReplicaSets. Fix: kubectl -n clh-match get pdb, then temporarily kubectl -n clh-match patch pdb match-engine -p '{"spec":{"minAvailable":8}}', wait the rollout, put it back to 10. Do not delete the PDB. We set minAvailable 10 after a January-adjacent event where we drained 6 at once and Kafka rebalanced for 38s. If you patch, leave a Slack note and a reminder to unpatch. I have forgotten once. Diego has a watch for pdb minAvailable != 10.
ImagePullBackOff on the old tag

ECR lifecycle. 30 images. If the last good tag is 31st, it is gone. Symptom: rollback --wait timeout, pods ImagePullBackOff. Do not rollback further into history hunting for a tag that exists. Check aws ecr describe-images --repository-name clh/match-engine --region us-east-1 --profile clh-prod. If missing, Jordan's backup, or rebuild the tag from the git sha in helm history DESCRIPTION (we put the sha there starting March 2024; January descriptions do not have it). Rebuilding at 02:00 is a Priya call.
break-svc talking to a rolled match-engine proto

break-svc 2.9.x speaks gRPC MatchEngine/Ack v3. match-engine 1.50+ serves v3. If you roll match-engine to something older than 1.50 and leave break-svc, Ack fails. We should not still have a 1.50-minus image in ECR that helm will accept. If we do, and you roll there, break-svc logs will show Unimplemented. Roll break-svc only if you know the pair. Safer: do not roll match-engine across a proto boundary. helm history CHART column plus the table in CLH-TDD-2024-006 (otel, but it has a proto appendix) or ask Kavya. If Kavya is asleep, do not cross 1.50.
Rejected shortcuts

blocks.caption: Ideas that showed up in Slack after January. They stay rejected.
rows: helm rollback --force every time, skip flyway
Aman, 06:44 Jan 11, by action if not by words
Schema diverged. Health lied. 41 extra minutes.
kubectl rollout undo deploy instead of helm rollback
Undo moves the ReplicaSet, not the ConfigMap, Jobs, or CR. Next helm upgrade then fights live state. We use helm for these three releases. Stay on helm.
Keep migrate Jobs out of helm, run flyway from Jenkins
Then the on-call cannot see SQL in the same history as the chart. Priya said no. Jenkins can still call helm.
Would have rolled us on January 11 into the Hibernate 500s faster. Not until we have a write-path SLO in the analysis. Spike closed.
Delete the CRD on rollback to 'start clean'
Deleted MatchEngineConfig CRD in staging, every namespace's CRs vanished. Do not. Delete extra CRs, never the CRD.

blocks.text: Checklist you can paste into Slack

items: context is clh-prod-eks-01 / 184920337661. Posted in #clh-deploys.
helm history read. Target revision number written down, not current-1 by habit.
migrate Job logs read. flyway_schema_history last 8 rows read. Safe or stop.
helm rollback <rel> <N> --wait --timeout ... --cleanup-on-fail.
rollout status green. /healthz green. write probe or CronJob smoke green.
kubectl get jobs, failed hook pods, matchengines, ingressroute. Delete junk only, not CRDs.
ConfigMap flags match the image. PDB minAvailable back to 10 if you patched.
Helen or Datadog: queue depth and lag moving the right way for 10 minutes before you leave the channel.
